docs.purpose: A running list of every document the product has generated and sent out — who exported what, when, and to whom. It is the record you reach for when a customer asks what was sent on their behalf, or when a compliance question lands. It is also the first place a broken export path becomes visible, because an export feature that no one ever uses shows up here as an empty list rather than as silence.
docs.data_story: Nothing is built yet, so nothing is measured here. As specified it would read `usage_events` and `exports` — of which `usage_events` and `exports` do **not exist yet** and must be declared, migrated and drift-asserted before this page can render a single row.
docs.under_126: **NEW.** It does not exist; it is generated from descriptors from its first commit, through the LIST renderer (a collection with declared pagination, recycling and empty/offline states). It is **100% generated** — which is the point: if the descriptor set is incomplete or an archetype profile is wrong, this page is visibly empty or visibly wrong on commit 1, and cannot be faked by hand.

checks.why: The row's whole point: a broken export path shows up here as an EMPTY LIST rather than as silence — the dead-meter defect made visible instead of repeated.
The LIST profile requires it; a desktop admin page keeps no cached projection, so this is descriptive.
A failed read must not render as "nothing was ever exported" on a compliance page.
R-23: a pdf_exports row with no pdf_send usage_events row means the meter did not fire, which is precisely the /api/leads/view defect — and this page is where it becomes visible on day one.
Rule 15: pdf_exports.parity_fingerprint is the golden fingerprint of the projection the PDF was rendered from, and this column is where the screen-vs-PDF comparison is read rather than promised.

The recipient column names a person who received a document; the projection must be an explicit pick-by-name whitelist, never a row spread, so a column added upstream cannot leak a PII field into an admin list by accident.
subject_kind and since are parameters of a stable key array.

invariants.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM pdf_exports WHERE expires_at IS NOT NULL AND expires_at <= (SELECT min(occurred_at) FROM usage_events u WHERE u.subject_key = pdf_exports.export_id::text)
invariants.why: An export that expired before it was issued is a clock or write-order defect, and a compliance list that renders it launders the defect into a plausible record.

invariants.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM pdf_exports WHERE subject_kind NOT IN ('parcel_ref','parcel_pk','permit_rev','offer_id')
invariants.why: R-04: this estate has two different things named parcel_id (parcels.id SERIAL vs parcels.parcel_id VARCHAR(20)), so an open subject_kind would silently blend them.

plausibility.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM usage_events WHERE event = 'pdf_send'
plausibility.why: A zero here means either "nobody exported anything" or "the meter is dead", and those are indistinguishable from a count alone — the measured trap that let a 153-line metered route with 44 passing tests and no callers survive for months. It is rendered beside the pdf_exports row count so the two can be compared.

plausibility.sql: SELECT min(bytes), percentile_disc(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY bytes), max(bytes) FROM pdf_exports
plausibility.why: A 0-byte or absurdly large PDF is the visible symptom of a renderer that failed silently; src/lib/export/pdf.ts today returns Buffer.from(html), which would land in exactly the wrong band.

limitations.what: The LIST required-field profile in Spec 126 §3.1 mandates list.item_archetype, list.pagination and list.recycling, and surface.schema.json has no property for any of them (the top level and every category are additionalProperties:false).
limitations.measured: Every allOf block in scripts/surfaces/_schema/surface.schema.json is `"then": true` — the archetype profiles are declared in prose in Spec 126 §3.1 and enforced by nothing, so these fields can neither be declared here nor caught missing.

limitations.what: render.export is "none" on an export-audit page.
limitations.measured: No spec declares a CSV or PDF export of this list; Spec 126 §6.5 governs the PDFs the page AUDITS, not the page itself. Inventing one would be a per-surface invention, so the field is "none" and the decision is named here.

TABLE NAME CORRECTED: the prior note and the source report both call the table `exports`; Spec 126 §6.3 row 7 names it `pdf_exports` and §6.3 closes ASK-09 with "Names are fixed here, before the first migration: placements, not offer_placements; pdf_exports, not exports", adding that migrate.js is filename-keyed so renaming after it ships costs a migration plus a data move.
